funFact: Cape cobras are highly venomous and are responsible for the most snakebite deaths in southern Africa.
description: The Cape cobra is one of the most dangerous cobras in Africa, found in the shrublands and fynbos of southern Africa. It is highly venomous with potent neurotoxin. It is a diurnal species and an excellent climber.

name: Crested Iguana
habitat: Dry forests and thorn scrub of western Madagascar
funFact: Crested iguanas can change color from green to black based on temperature and social context.
description: The crested iguana is a critically endangered species endemic to the dry forests of western Madagascar. It has a distinctive high dorsal crest and is one of the rarest iguanas in the world. It is primarily herbivorous, feeding on leaves and fruit.

name: Argentine Black and White Tegu
habitat: Grasslands, savannas, and forests of South America
funFact: Argentine tegus can regulate their body temperature during the reproductive season without relying solely on external heat.
description: The Argentine black and white tegu is a large, omnivorous lizard native to South America. It has distinctive black and white banding and a robust body. It feeds on a wide variety of foods including insects, small animals, fruit, and eggs.

name: King Brown Snake
habitat: Woodlands, forests, and grasslands of Australia
funFact: The king brown snake is technically a black snake, not a brown snake, and is in the genus Pseudechis.
description: The king brown snake, also known as the mulga snake, is one of Australia's most widespread and dangerous snakes. Despite its name, it belongs to the black snake genus Pseudechis. It is responsible for more snakebite deaths in Australia than any other species.

name: False Gharial
habitat: Freshwater rivers and swamps of Southeast Asia
funFact: The false gharial has a narrow snout similar to the true gharial but is not closely related to it.
description: The false gharial is a critically endangered crocodilian found in the rivers and swamps of Southeast Asia. It has a distinctive long, narrow snout and is one of the largest crocodilian species. It is a specialist fish-eater with a unique jaw structure.

name: Indian Star Tortoise
habitat: Dry scrublands and grasslands of India and Sri Lanka
funFact: Indian star tortoises have star-shaped patterns on their shells that help with camouflage and thermoregulation.
description: The Indian star tortoise is a small to medium-sized tortoise native to India and Sri Lanka. It has distinctive star-shaped patterns on its carapace that radiate from the center of each scute. It is a popular species in the illegal pet trade.

name: Green Anaconda
habitat: Swamps, marshes, and slow-moving rivers of South America
funFact: The green anaconda is the heaviest snake in the world, with some individuals weighing over 220 pounds.
description: The green anaconda is the heaviest and one of the longest snakes in the world, found in the swamps and rivers of South America. It is a non-venomous constrictor that feeds on deer, capybaras, and even jaguars. It spends most of its time in water.

name: Tuatara
habitat: Offshore islands and forested areas of New Zealand
funFact: Tuatara are the last surviving members of an order of reptiles that lived alongside dinosaurs over 200 million years ago.
description: The tuatara is a reptile endemic to New Zealand and the only surviving member of the order Rhynchocephalia. Often called a living fossil, it has remained virtually unchanged for 200 million years. It has a third eye on top of its head that detects light changes.

name: Eastern Water Dragon
habitat: Rivers, creeks, and wetlands of eastern Australia
funFact: Eastern water dragons can swim underwater for up to 90 minutes, closing a special membrane to keep water out of their eyes.
description: The eastern water dragon is a large agamid lizard found along rivers and creeks in eastern Australia. Males have a distinctive red chest and a spiny crest along their back. It is semi-aquatic and an excellent swimmer.

name: Spider Tortoise
habitat: Dry spiny forests of southern Madagascar
funFact: Spider tortoises are named for the radiating yellow lines on their shells that resemble a spider's web.
description: The spider tortoise is a critically endangered species endemic to the dry spiny forests of southern Madagascar. It has distinctive yellow radiating patterns on its dark shell that resemble a spider's web. It is one of the smallest tortoise species in the world.

name: Russian Tortoise
habitat: Arid grasslands and steppes of Central Asia
funFact: Russian tortoises can survive extreme temperatures by brumating underground for up to 6 months during harsh winters.
description: The Russian tortoise is a small species native to the arid steppes of Central Asia. It is one of the most cold-tolerant tortoise species, surviving harsh winters by brumating underground. It is popular in the pet trade due to its small size and hardy nature.

name: Ball Python
habitat: Grasslands and savannas of western and central Africa
funFact: Ball pythons curl into a tight ball with their head protected in the center when frightened, hence their name.
description: The ball python is a non-venomous constrictor native to the grasslands of western and central Africa. It is the most popular pet snake in the world due to its docile temperament and manageable size. It has hundreds of color morphs bred in captivity.

name: Cat-Eyed Snake
habitat: Tropical rainforests and cloud forests of Central and South America
funFact: Cat-eyed snakes have vertical pupils like cats, giving them excellent night vision for hunting in the dark rainforest.
description: The cat-eyed snake is a small, rear-fanged snake found in the tropical rainforests of Central and South America. It has distinctive vertical pupils and is primarily nocturnal. It feeds on frogs, lizards, and small mammals.

name: Arabian Chameleon
habitat: Arid shrublands and gardens of the Arabian Peninsula
funFact: Arabian chameleons are one of the few chameleon species adapted to live in hot, arid desert conditions.
description: The Arabian chameleon is a species of chameleon native to the Arabian Peninsula. It is adapted to arid conditions, unlike most chameleon species. It has a casque on its head and can change color for communication and thermoregulation.

name: Spotted Turtle
habitat: Shallow, slow-moving waters of eastern North America
funFact: Spotted turtles have yellow spots on their dark shells that become more numerous with age, like counting tree rings.
description: The spotted turtle is one of the smallest turtles in North America, found in shallow, slow-moving waters. It has a smooth, dark shell with distinctive yellow or orange spots. It is a long-lived species that can survive for over a century.

name: Banded Krait
habitat: Rice paddies, forests, and plains of South and Southeast Asia
funFact: Banded kraits are twice as venomous as cobras and often cannibalize other snakes, including other kraits.
description: The banded krait is a highly venomous elapid found in South and Southeast Asia. It has distinctive black and yellow bands and is primarily nocturnal. It feeds on other snakes, including venomous species, and is responsible for many snakebite deaths in Asia.

name: Golden Skink
habitat: Tropical forests and gardens of South and Southeast Asia
funFact: Golden skinks have a metallic, iridescent sheen that makes them look like they are coated in gold.
description: The golden skink is a small, fast-moving lizard found in tropical forests and gardens across South and Southeast Asia. It has a metallic, iridescent body that gives it a golden appearance. It is diurnal and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

name: Broad-Snouted Caiman
habitat: Freshwater lakes, marshes, and slow-moving rivers of South America
funFact: Broad-snouted caimans build mounds of vegetation to incubate their eggs, using decomposition heat to warm them.
description: The broad-snouted caiman is a medium-sized crocodilian found in the freshwater habitats of South America. It has a broad, flat snout adapted for catching fish and invertebrates. It builds vegetation mounds to incubate its eggs.

name: Copperhead
habitat: Forests, rocky hillsides, and mixed woodlands of eastern North America
funFact: Copperheads account for the majority of venomous snakebites in the United States, though their venom is rarely fatal.
description: The copperhead is a venomous pit viper found across the eastern United States. It has a distinctive copper-colored head and hourglass-shaped crossbands. It is responsible for the most snakebite cases in North America, though fatalities are rare.

name: Radiated Tortoise
habitat: Dry spiny forests and grasslands of southern Madagascar
funFact: Radiated tortoises can live for over 100 years, with some individuals reportedly reaching 188 years of age.
description: The radiated tortoise is a critically endangered species endemic to Madagascar. It has a high-domed shell with striking yellow star-shaped patterns radiating from the center of each scute. It is threatened by habitat loss and poaching for food and the pet trade.

name: Blue Racer
habitat: Prairies, open woodlands, and farmlands of the central United States
funFact: Blue racers are one of the fastest snakes in North America, capable of speeds up to 10 mph.
description: The blue racer is a fast-moving, non-venomous colubrid found across the central United States and southern Ontario. It has a distinctive blue-grey dorsal color and a white or cream underside. It is diurnal and feeds on rodents, frogs, and other snakes.

name: Side-Blotched Lizard
habitat: Deserts, grasslands, and scrublands of western North America
funFact: Male side-blotched lizards use a rock-paper-scissors strategy with three throat colors to compete for mates.
description: The side-blotched lizard is a small lizard found in the deserts and grasslands of western North America. It is famous in evolutionary biology for its rock-paper-scissors mating strategy. Males have three throat colors that correspond to different mating tactics.

name: Nile Monitor
habitat: Rivers, lakes, and marshes throughout sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: Nile monitors are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath for up to an hour while submerged underwater.
description: The Nile monitor is a large, powerful lizard found throughout sub-Saharan Africa near water. It is semi-aquatic and feeds on fish, frogs, birds, eggs, and carrion. It has a forked tongue used for detecting prey in the water.

name: Canebrake Rattlesnake
habitat: Forests, canebrakes, and swamps of the southeastern United States
funFact: Canebrake rattlesnakes have a silent rattle compared to other rattlesnake species, often delivering strikes without warning.
description: The canebrake rattlesnake, a subspecies of the timber rattlesnake, is found in the forests and swamps of the southeastern United States. It has a distinctive pinkish-brown color with dark crossbands. It is a dangerous venomous pit viper.

name: Yellow-Footed Tortoise
habitat: Tropical rainforests of the Amazon Basin
funFact: Yellow-footed tortoises play a crucial role in seed dispersal in the Amazon, helping to regenerate the rainforest.
description: The yellow-footed tortoise is a medium-sized tortoise native to the Amazon Basin of South America. It has distinctive yellow or orange scales on its legs and head. It feeds primarily on fallen fruit and plays an important ecological role in seed dispersal.

name: Puff Adder
habitat: Savannas, grasslands, and scrublands of sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: Puff adders are responsible for more snakebite deaths in Africa than any other snake due to their excellent camouflage.
description: The puff adder is a venomous viper found throughout sub-Saharan Africa. It relies on its excellent camouflage and will not flee when approached, leading to many defensive strikes. It is an ambush predator that strikes with incredible speed.

name: Red-Eared Slider
habitat: Ponds, lakes, and rivers of the Mississippi Valley and Gulf Coast
funFact: Red-eared sliders are the most widely distributed turtle species in the world, considered one of the top 100 invasive species globally.
description: The red-eared slider is a semi-aquatic turtle native to the Mississippi Valley region of the United States. It is the most popular pet turtle in the world and has become a significant invasive species on every continent except Antarctica. It has a distinctive red stripe behind each eye.

name: Eastern Green Mamba
habitat: Coastal forests and woodlands of eastern and southern Africa
funFact: Eastern green mambas are arboreal and rarely descend to the ground, spending their lives in the forest canopy.
description: The eastern green mamba is a fast, highly venomous elapid found in the coastal forests of eastern and southern Africa. It is bright green, blending perfectly with the forest canopy. Unlike the black mamba, it is arboreal and rarely comes to the ground.

name: Cape Dwarf Chameleon
habitat: Shrublands, gardens, and fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa
funFact: Cape dwarf chameleons have independently moving eyes that can rotate 180 degrees, giving them a 360-degree field of vision.
description: The Cape dwarf chameleon is a small chameleon endemic to the Western Cape of South Africa. It has independently rotating eyes, a prehensile tail, and a long, sticky tongue for catching insects. It can change color for communication and thermoregulation.

name: Chinese Alligator
habitat: Freshwater rivers, lakes, and wetlands of eastern China
funFact: Chinese alligators are the most endangered crocodilian species, with fewer than 150 individuals remaining in the wild.
description: The Chinese alligator is a critically endangered species, one of only two alligator species in the world. Found in eastern China, it is smaller than the American alligator and has bony plates on its eyelids. Wild populations are critically low.

name: Snouted Cobra
habitat: Savannas, grasslands, and coastal bush of southern Africa
funFact: Snouted cobras can spit venom accurately up to 2 meters, aiming for the eyes of perceived threats.
description: The snouted cobra is a large, highly venomous snake found across southern Africa. It has a distinctive upturned snout and can spit venom accurately. It is found in a wide variety of habitats and feeds on rodents, birds, and other snakes.

name: Common Wall Lizard
habitat: Stone walls, rocky outcrops, and urban areas of Europe
funFact: Common wall lizards have been introduced to North America from Europe and are now thriving in cities like Toronto and Vancouver.
description: The common wall lizard is a small, agile lizard found across Europe and introduced to North America. It is commonly seen basking on stone walls and buildings. It feeds on insects, spiders, and small invertebrates.

name: Brown Tree Snake
habitat: Forests, shrublands, and human structures in Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Guam
funFact: The brown tree snake has driven at least 10 bird species to extinction on Guam after accidentally introduced there.
description: The brown tree snake is an arboreal, rear-fanged snake native to Australia and New Guinea. It has become one of the world's most destructive invasive species on Guam, where it has eliminated most of the island's native bird species. It is nocturnal and feeds on birds, lizards, and mammals.

name: Angulate Tortoise
habitat: Fynbos and karoo shrublands of South Africa and Namibia
funFact: Angulate tortoises are the most southerly distributed tortoise species in Africa, found even in the cool, wet Western Cape.
description: The angulate tortoise is a small tortoise found in the fynbos and karoo shrublands of southern Africa. It has a distinctive upturned front margin to its shell. It is well adapted to the Mediterranean climate of the Western Cape region.

name: Savannah Monitor
habitat: Savannas, woodlands, and grasslands of sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: Savannah monitors can slow their metabolism so much that they can survive on as few as three large meals per year.
description: The savannah monitor is a medium-sized monitor lizard found across sub-Saharan Africa. It is a ground-dwelling species that digs burrows for shelter. It feeds on insects, small mammals, and reptiles, and is popular in the exotic pet trade.

name: White-Lipped Pit Viper
habitat: Tropical rainforests and bamboo groves of Southeast Asia
funFact: White-lipped pit vipers have heat-sensing pits between their eyes and nostrils that detect warm-blooded prey in complete darkness.
description: The white-lipped pit viper is a venomous snake found in the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia. It has a distinctive white or yellow line along its upper lip and is primarily arboreal. It is a nocturnal ambush predator that feeds on rodents and birds.

name: Alabama Red-Bellied Cooter
habitat: Rivers, lakes, and ponds of Alabama and Georgia
funFact: Alabama red-bellied cooters can bask for hours, using the sun to synthesize vitamin D3 for shell health.
description: The Alabama red-bellied cooter is an endangered freshwater turtle endemic to Alabama and Georgia. It has a dark shell with a distinctive red or orange plastron. It is found in rivers, lakes, and ponds with abundant aquatic vegetation.

name: Amazon Tree Boa
habitat: Tropical rainforests of the Amazon Basin, arboreal
funFact: Amazon tree boas are incredibly variable in color and pattern, with no two individuals looking exactly alike.
description: The Amazon tree boa is a small, arboreal constrictor found throughout the Amazon rainforest. It is nocturnal and feeds on birds and small mammals. It has an extremely variable color pattern, ranging from yellow to red to brown.

name: California Kingsnake
habitat: Deserts, grasslands, forests, and suburban areas of the western United States
funFact: California kingsnakes are immune to rattlesnake venom and regularly prey upon rattlesnakes in the wild.
description: The California kingsnake is a popular, non-venomous constrictor found across the western United States. It has a banded pattern of brown and white or yellow. It is an opportunistic feeder that readily eats rattlesnakes, making it beneficial to humans.

name: Clouded Monitor
funFact: Clouded monitors are arboreal and have sharp claws that allow them to climb vertical tree trunks with ease.
description: The clouded monitor is a medium-sized monitor lizard found in the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia. It is arboreal and has a long, slender body adapted for climbing. It feeds on insects, small mammals, and birds.

name: Brazilian Rainbow Boa
habitat: Tropical rainforests of the Amazon and Orinoco Basins
funFact: Brazilian rainbow boas have iridescent scales that create a holographic rainbow effect when exposed to light.
description: The Brazilian rainbow boa is a medium-sized, non-venomous constrictor found in the rainforests of South America. Its name comes from the stunning iridescent sheen of its scales. It is primarily terrestrial and feeds on rodents, birds, and bats.

name: Northern Cuirassated Lizard
habitat: Rocky hillsides and scrublands of Mexico
funFact: Northern cuirassated lizards have bony armor plates called osteoderms that provide protection from predators.
description: The northern cuirassated lizard is a small lizard found in the rocky hillsides of Mexico. It has distinctive bony armor plates called osteoderms covering its body. It is diurnal and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

name: Desert Iguana
habitat: Sonoran and Mojave Deserts of the southwestern United States
funFact: Desert iguanas can tolerate body temperatures up to 120°F, making them one of the most heat-tolerant lizards.
description: The desert iguana is a medium-sized lizard found in the deserts of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It is one of the most heat-tolerant lizards, active at temperatures that force other reptiles to seek shade. It feeds primarily on leaves and flowers.

name: False Water Cobra
habitat: Wetlands, marshes, and riverine forests of South America
funFact: False water cobras flatten their necks like true cobras when threatened, despite being only mildly venomous.
description: The false water cobra is a large, semi-aquatic colubrid found in the wetlands of South America. It displays a cobra-like hood when threatened, despite being only mildly venomous. It is an excellent swimmer and feeds on fish, frogs, and small mammals.

name: Common Garter Snake
habitat: Gardens, woodlands, and meadows across North America
funFact: Garter snakes are mildly venomous but harmless to humans, making them one of the most common backyard snakes.
description: The common garter snake is one of the most widespread snakes in North America, found in gardens, meadows, and woodlands. It has distinctive longitudinal stripes. Despite being mildly venomous, it is harmless to humans and beneficial as pest control.

name: Shingleback Skink
habitat: Woodlands, grasslands, and heathlands of southern Australia
funFact: Shingleback skinks mate for life and reunite with the same partner every breeding season.
description: The shingleback skink is a large, slow-moving lizard found in the woodlands and grasslands of southern Australia. It has rough, pinecone-like scales and a short, fat tail that resembles its head, confusing predators. It is one of the few reptile species that mate for life.

name: Thorny Devil
habitat: Arid spinifex grasslands and deserts of central Australia
funFact: Thorny devils have micro-channels in their skin that funnel water from any body part directly to their mouths.
description: The thorny devil is a small, spiny lizard native to the arid deserts of central Australia. Its entire body is covered in conical spines that provide defense against predators. Its skin has microscopic channels that collect water and transport it to its mouth.

name: Mozambique Spitting Cobra
habitat: Savannas, woodlands, and coastal forests of eastern and southern Africa
funFact: Mozambique spitting cobras can spit venom accurately up to 3 meters, targeting the eyes of threats.
description: The Mozambique spitting cobra is a highly venomous elapid found across eastern and southern Africa. It is one of the most dangerous snakes in the region, responsible for many snakebite cases. It can spit venom accurately into the eyes of perceived threats.

name: American Bullfrog
habitat: Ponds, lakes, slow-moving streams, and wetlands
funFact: American Bullfrogs can eat almost anything they can fit in their mouths, including other frogs, birds, and even snakes.
description: The American Bullfrog is the largest frog in North America. They are powerful swimmers and aggressive predators, known for their deep jug-o-rum calls that can be heard up to a mile away.

name: Red-Eyed Tree Frog
habitat: Tropical rainforest canopies near rivers and ponds
funFact: Red-Eyed Tree Frogs flash their bright red eyes to startle predators, giving them a chance to escape.
description: The Red-Eyed Tree Frog is one of the most iconic rainforest amphibians. With vibrant green bodies, blue and yellow striped sides, and stunning red eyes, they are a symbol of tropical biodiversity.

name: Blue Poison Dart Frog
funFact: Blue Poison Dart Frogs derive their toxicity from the ants and mites they eat in the wild.
description: The Blue Poison Dart Frog is a small, brilliantly colored amphibian found in the rainforests of Suriname. Their vivid blue coloration warns predators of their potent skin toxins.

name: Golden Poison Dart Frog
funFact: A single Golden Poison Dart Frog carries enough toxin to kill 10 grown men.
description: The Golden Poison Dart Frog is the most toxic vertebrate on Earth. Found only in Colombia, its bright yellow skin contains batrachotoxin, a potent neurotoxin used by indigenous people to poison blowgun darts.

name: Glass Frog
habitat: Cloud forests and tropical rainforests near streams
funFact: Glass Frogs have transparent abdominal skin that allows you to see their beating heart and internal organs.
description: Glass Frogs are remarkable amphibians with translucent ventral skin. Found in Central and South America, they spend most of their lives in trees and descend only to breed near fast-flowing streams.

name: Pacman Frog
habitat: Grasslands and shallow burrows in warm climates
funFact: Pacman Frogs are named after the video game character due to their enormous mouths and round bodies.
description: The Pacman Frog, also known as the Argentine Horned Frog, is a popular pet species known for its large mouth and sedentary lifestyle. They are ambush predators that sit and wait for prey to pass by.

name: Budgett's Frog
funFact: Budgett's Frogs inflate their bodies and scream when threatened to appear larger and more intimidating.
description: Budgett's Frog is a flattened, broad-bodied frog found in South America. They are known for their aggressive defensive behavior, including inflating, screaming, and biting when disturbed.

name: White's Tree Frog
habitat: Tree hollows and foliage near water sources
funFact: White's Tree Frogs have fatty deposits above their eyes that look like eyebrows, giving them a perpetual smile.
description: White's Tree Frog, also known as the Dumpy Tree Frog, is one of the most docile and popular amphibian pets. Native to Australia and New Guinea, they are known for their placid temperament and ability to thrive in captivity.

name: African Dwarf Frog
habitat: Streams, rivers, and ponds in sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: African Dwarf Frogs are fully aquatic and spend their entire lives underwater, unlike most frogs.
description: African Dwarf Frogs are tiny, fully aquatic amphibians that never leave the water. They are social creatures that do best in groups and are popular aquarium pets due to their small size and active nature.

name: Amazon Milk Frog
funFact: Amazon Milk Frogs secrete a milky white toxin when threatened and can change color from light to dark blue.
description: The Amazon Milk Frog is a large tree frog found in the Amazon rainforest. They have a distinctive black and white or blue and white banded pattern and are named for the milky toxic substance they secrete.

name: Gray Tree Frog
funFact: Gray Tree Frogs can change color from gray to green depending on their environment and activity level.
description: The Gray Tree Frog is a small, arboreal frog native to eastern North America. They have bumpy skin that resembles tree bark and bright yellow-orange patches on the inside of their hind legs.

name: Spring Peeper
habitat: Forests near marshes, ponds, and vernal pools
funFact: The Spring Peeper's high-pitched peeping call can be heard from over a mile away during breeding season.
description: Spring Peepers are tiny tree frogs whose chorus marks the arrival of spring in eastern North America. Their characteristic X-shaped marking on their back helps identify them among other small frogs.

name: Wood Frog
funFact: Wood Frogs can survive being frozen solid, with up to 65% of their body water turning to ice.
description: Wood Frogs are remarkable for their ability to freeze during winter and thaw out alive in spring. Found across North America, they have a distinctive dark mask marking behind each eye.

name: American Toad
funFact: A single American Toad can eat up to 1,000 insects per day, making them excellent garden pest controllers.
description: The American Toad is one of the most common and widespread toads in North America. They have warty skin, parotoid glands that produce a mild toxin, and can live for over a decade in the wild.

name: Cane Toad
habitat: Open habitats, farms, and disturbed areas
funFact: Cane Toads were introduced to Australia in 1935 to control beetles but became one of the worst invasive species in the world.
description: The Cane Toad is a large, toxic toad native to Central and South America. It has become one of the most successful invasive amphibians, spreading across Australia, the Caribbean, and Pacific islands.

name: Fire-Bellied Toad
funFact: Fire-Bellied Toads display their bright orange-red bellies when threatened in a behavior called the unken reflex.
description: Fire-Bellied Toads are small, semi-aquatic toads with bumpy olive-green backs and vivid orange or red bellies. They are popular pets and are known for their aposematic coloration that warns predators of their toxins.

name: Desert Rain Frog
habitat: Coastal sand dunes and sandy soils
funFact: Desert Rain Frogs let out a high-pitched squeak when threatened, sounding like a dog toy.
description: The Desert Rain Frog is a tiny, round frog that burrows into sand along the coast of South Africa and Namibia. They spend most of their lives underground and emerge only to feed and breed during foggy conditions.

name: Goliath Frog
funFact: The Goliath Frog is the largest living frog in the world, weighing up to 7 pounds and spanning over a foot long.
description: The Goliath Frog, or Conraua goliath, is the world's largest frog. Found only in Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea, these massive amphibians inhabit fast-flowing rivers and are threatened by habitat loss and hunting.

name: Mountain Chicken Frog
funFact: Despite their name, Mountain Chicken Frogs are not chickens but are called so because their leg meat tastes like chicken.
description: The Mountain Chicken Frog is one of the largest frogs in the Caribbean, found only on Dominica and Montserrat. They are critically endangered due to the chytrid fungus and habitat destruction.

name: Spadefoot Toad
funFact: Spadefoot Toads can burrow underground and remain dormant for up to nine months, emerging only when it rains.
description: Spadefoot Toads are adapted to arid environments with specialized keratinized spades on their hind feet for burrowing. They spend most of their lives underground and breed explosively in temporary rain pools.

name: Natterjack Toad
habitat: Sandy dunes, heathlands, and coastal areas
funFact: Natterjack Toads are one of the loudest European amphibians, with calls that can be heard over a mile away.
description: The Natterjack Toad is a medium-sized toad found across Europe. Unlike most toads, they run rather than hop and are known for their loud, rasping calls during breeding season.

name: Midwife Toad
funFact: Male Midwife Toads carry the eggs wrapped around their hind legs until they are ready to hatch.
description: Midwife Toads are small, nocturnal toads named for the male's paternal behavior of carrying eggs on his hind legs. Found across Europe, they have a distinctive high-pitched beep-like call.

name: European Tree Frog
funFact: European Tree Frogs have adhesive toe pads that allow them to climb smooth surfaces, including glass.
description: The European Tree Frog is a small, bright green frog with a distinctive dark stripe along each side. They are excellent climbers and are often found in gardens, orchards, and damp woodlands.

name: Leopard Frog
funFact: Leopard Frogs can jump up to 20 times their body length in a single leap.
description: The Leopard Frog gets its name from the distinctive dark spots covering its green or brown body. Found across North America, they are strong jumpers and swimmers that inhabit a variety of wetland habitats.

name: Strawberry Poison Dart Frog
funFact: The Strawberry Poison Dart Frog has over 30 color morphs, ranging from red with blue legs to green with yellow spots.
description: The Strawberry Poison Dart Frog, also known as the Blue Jeans Frog, is a small but vividly colored amphibian found in Central America. Males carry tadpoles on their backs to suitable pools of water.

name: Dyeing Poison Dart Frog
funFact: The Dyeing Poison Dart Frog was named because indigenous people used its toxins to dye fabric.
description: The Dyeing Poison Dart Frog is a variable species with striking color patterns. Found in South America, they were named for the use of their skin secretions by indigenous peoples to dye feathers and textiles.

name: Harlequin Toad
funFact: Many Harlequin Toad species were thought to be extinct until small populations were rediscovered in recent years.
description: Harlequin Toads are a diverse group of brightly colored toads found in Central and South America. Many species are critically endangered or believed extinct due to the chytrid fungus and habitat loss.

name: Pickerel Frog
habitat: Cool streams, springs, and boggy areas
funFact: Pickerel Frogs produce a toxin that can irritate human skin and is lethal to other frogs.
description: The Pickerel Frog is a brownish frog with two parallel rows of dark rectangular spots down its back. Found in eastern North America, they are one of the few frogs whose skin secretions are toxic to other amphibians.

name: Cherry Tree Frog
funFact: Cherry Tree Frogs can change color from bright green to brown depending on their surroundings.
description: The Cherry Tree Frog is a small European tree frog known for its distinctive call that sounds like a cherry pit being clicked. They are excellent climbers with adhesive toe pads.

name: Asian Common Toad
habitat: Gardens, agricultural areas, and urban environments
funFact: Asian Common Toads are extremely adaptable and thrive in human-modified environments across Southeast Asia.
description: The Asian Common Toad is a widespread toad found across South and Southeast Asia. They are highly adaptable to urban environments and are often found in gardens, drains, and agricultural areas.

name: Clown Tree Frog
funFact: Clown Tree Frogs are named for their playful, acrobatic movements through the trees.
description: The Clown Tree Frog is a colorful, medium-sized tree frog found in the Amazon rainforest. They have striking patterns of brown, green, and cream that provide excellent camouflage against tree bark.

name: Gliding Tree Frog
funFact: Gliding Tree Frogs can spread their enlarged toe pads and webbed feet to glide between trees.
description: The Gliding Tree Frog has evolved enlarged adhesive toe pads and partially webbed feet that allow it to glide through the rainforest canopy. Found in Central America, they are active at night.

name: Black-Legged Poison Frog
funFact: Black-Legged Poison Frogs exhibit biparental care, with both parents tending to their eggs and tadpoles.
description: The Black-Legged Poison Frog is a small, toxic frog found in the rainforests of Colombia. They are known for their complex parental care behaviors and striking black and yellow coloration.

name: Red-Backed Poison Frog
funFact: Red-Backed Poison Frogs use their bright coloration to warn predators of their skin toxins in a strategy called aposematism.
description: The Red-Backed Poison Frog is a small, brightly colored amphibian found in the Amazon rainforest. Their vivid red or orange back serves as a warning to potential predators.

name: Splashback Poison Frog
funFact: Splashback Poison Frogs get their name from their colorful backs that look like paint splashes.
description: The Splashback Poison Frog is a small amphibian with vivid coloration that varies from green to blue to yellow. Found in South America, they carry tadpoles on their backs to water-filled bromeliads.

name: Cane Turtle Frog
funFact: Cane Turtle Frogs have a flattened body shape that allows them to hide under rocks and logs.
description: The Cane Turtle Frog is a small, flattened frog found in South America. They are often found in agricultural areas, particularly sugarcane fields, and have a distinctive flattened appearance.

name: Malaysian Horned Frog
funFact: Malaysian Horned Frogs have horn-like projections above their eyes that help break up their outline among leaf litter.
description: The Malaysian Horned Frog is a medium-sized frog with distinctive horn-like projections above each eye. Found in Southeast Asian rainforests, they are well-camouflaged among dead leaves on the forest floor.

name: Hampire Poison Dart Frog
funFact: Hampire Poison Dart Frogs are named after the Harry Potter character due to their striking black and orange pattern.
description: The Hamphire Poison Dart Frog is a small, strikingly colored amphibian found in South America. Their bold pattern serves as a warning to predators of their toxic skin secretions.

name: Brazilian Horned Frog
funFact: Brazilian Horned Frogs are ambush predators that can remain motionless for hours waiting for prey.
description: The Brazilian Horned Frog is a medium-sized frog with horn-like projections above its eyes. Found in the Amazon rainforest, they are well-camouflaged and lie in wait to ambush passing prey.

name: Hairy Frog
funFact: Male Hairy Frogs grow hair-like skin projections during breeding season to help absorb oxygen from water.
description: The Hairy Frog, also known as the Trichobatrachus, is a unique amphibian found in Central Africa. Males develop hair-like dermal papillae on their flanks and thighs during the breeding season.

name: Tomato Frog
funFact: Tomato Frogs secrete a thick, white substance that can glue a predator's mouth shut.
description: The Tomato Frog is a bright red-orange frog found in Madagascar. When threatened, they inflate their bodies and secrete a sticky white substance that can temporarily immobilize predators.

name: Marsupial Frog
funFact: Female Marsupial Frogs carry their eggs in a pouch on their back, similar to marsupial mammals.
description: The Marsupial Frog is a remarkable amphibian found in the Andes mountains. Females have a dorsal pouch where they carry their eggs until they develop into froglets, bypassing the tadpole stage.

name: Foam Nest Frog
funFact: Foam Nest Frogs create a frothy nest by beating their hind legs to whip up a foam that protects their eggs.
description: Foam Nest Frogs are found across Africa and South America. They are named for their unique breeding behavior where both sexes whip up a foam nest to protect their eggs from drying out.

name: Surinam Toad
habitat: Muddy bottoms of shallow rivers and ponds
funFact: Female Surinam Toads have eggs embedded in the skin of their backs, where they develop into froglets.
description: The Surinam Toad is a flat, bottom-dwelling amphibian found in South America. Females have a remarkable reproductive strategy where eggs are embedded in the skin of their backs until they emerge as fully formed froglets.

name: Painted Frog
funFact: Painted Frogs can tolerate brackish water and are sometimes found in coastal habitats.
description: The Painted Frog is a medium-sized frog found in the Mediterranean region. They have a distinctive appearance with mottled brown and green coloring and can tolerate slightly saline conditions.

name: Incredible Frog
funFact: The Incredible Frog can extend its fingers and toes to slow its descent when jumping from high branches.
description: The Incredible Frog is a small tree frog found in the rainforests of Central America. They have specialized finger and toe pads that allow them to control their descent when jumping between trees.

name: Axolotl
funFact: Axolotls can regenerate entire limbs, spinal cords, hearts, and even parts of their brains throughout their lives.
description: The Axolotl is a neotenic salamander that retains its larval features throughout life, including external gills. Found only in Lake Xochimilco in Mexico, it is critically endangered in the wild but widely bred in captivity.

name: Tiger Salamander
funFact: Tiger Salamanders are one of the longest-lived amphibians, with some individuals living over 20 years in captivity.
description: The Tiger Salamander is the largest terrestrial salamander in North America. They have distinctive yellow or olive markings on a dark background and spend most of their lives underground in burrows.

name: Eastern Newt
funFact: The juvenile Eastern Newt, called a red eft, is brightly colored to warn predators of its toxins.
description: The Eastern Newt has a complex life cycle with three distinct stages: aquatic larva, terrestrial red eft, and aquatic adult. Found in eastern North America, they produce tetrodotoxin in their skin.

name: Hellbender
habitat: Clean, fast-flowing streams with rocky bottoms
funFact: Hellbenders absorb oxygen through their wrinkly skin and are an indicator species for water quality.
description: The Hellbender is the largest salamander in North America, reaching up to two feet long. Found in clean, fast-flowing streams of the eastern United States, they are declining due to pollution and habitat loss.

name: Olm
funFact: Olms can survive without food for up to 10 years and are among the longest-lived amphibians.
description: The Olm is a blind, cave-dwelling salamander found in the caves of southern Europe. It has no eyes, is depigmented, and can live for over 100 years, making it one of the longest-lived vertebrates.

name: Fire Salamander
habitat: Deciduous forests near streams and ponds
funFact: Fire Salamanders were once believed to be born from fire and could extinguish flames with their cold bodies.
description: The Fire Salamander is one of Europe's most recognizable amphibians with its striking black body and bright yellow or orange markings. Found in central and southern Europe, they secrete samandarin, a neurotoxin.

name: Spotted Salamander
funFact: Spotted Salamanders have a symbiotic relationship with algae that lives inside their cells.
description: The Spotted Salamander is a large, robust salamander found in eastern North America. They have distinctive yellow spots on a dark background and are one of the few vertebrates known to have algae living inside their cells.

name: Red-Backed Salamander
habitat: Forests under logs, rocks, and leaf litter
funFact: Red-Backed Salamanders breathe entirely through their skin and have no lungs or gills as adults.
description: The Red-Backed Salamander is the most common and abundant salamander in eastern North America. They are entirely lungless, breathing through their moist skin, and come in both red-backed and lead-backed color phases.

name: Mudpuppy
habitat: Ponds, rivers, and lakes with muddy bottoms
funFact: Mudpuppies retain their external gills throughout their entire lives, a condition called neoteny.
description: The Mudpuppy is a fully aquatic salamander found in eastern North America. They retain their bushy red external gills throughout life and are nocturnal hunters that use sensory barbels to find prey.

name: Rough-Skinned Newt
funFact: Rough-Skinned Newts produce enough tetrodotoxin to kill several adult humans.
description: The Rough-Skinned Newt is a highly toxic amphibian found along the Pacific coast of North America. They produce tetrodotoxin, the same toxin found in pufferfish, and advertise their toxicity with bright orange undersides.

name: Alpine Salamander
funFact: Alpine Salamanders are entirely viviparous, giving birth to fully developed young rather than laying eggs.
description: The Alpine Salamander is found in the mountains of central and southern Europe. Unlike most amphibians, they give birth to live young that have completed their development inside the mother's body.

name: Great Crested Newt
habitat: Ponds, lakes, and surrounding terrestrial habitats
funFact: Male Great Crested Newts develop a jagged crest along their back during breeding season.
description: The Great Crested Newt is the largest newt species in Europe. Males develop a distinctive crest during breeding season and have a white flash on their tail. They are legally protected in many countries.

name: Marbled Salamander
funFact: Female Marbled Salamanders stay with their eggs and guard them until they hatch.
description: The Marbled Salamander is a small, stocky salamander with distinctive white or gray crossbands on a dark background. Found in eastern North America, they are one of the few salamanders that guard their eggs.

name: Long-Toed Salamander
funFact: Long-Toed Salamanders can have up to 13 toes on their hind feet, more than most salamanders.
description: The Long-Toed Salamander is a small salamander found across western North America. They have a characteristic stripe running down their back and long toes that give them their name.

name: Slimy Salamander
habitat: Deciduous forests under logs and rocks
funFact: Slimy Salamanders secrete a sticky, glue-like substance from their skin that is difficult to remove.
description: The Slimy Salamander is a medium-sized lungless salamander found in the eastern United States. They secrete a sticky white substance from their skin that helps deter predators.

name: Red Salamander
funFact: Red Salamanders are one of the largest lungless salamanders in North America.
description: The Red Salamander is a brightly colored amphibian found in the Appalachian region of the eastern United States. Adults have a distinctive red to orange coloration with scattered black spots.

name: Lesser Siren
funFact: Lesser Sirens can breathe through their gills and also through their skin, and can survive drying by burrowing into mud.
description: The Lesser Siren is a fully aquatic salamander with external gills found in the southeastern United States. They lack hind legs and can survive drought by burrowing into mud and entering a dormant state.

name: Greater Siren
funFact: Greater Sirens are the largest species in the Sirenidae family and can exceed three feet in length.
description: The Greater Siren is a large, fully aquatic salamander with external gills found in the coastal plains of the southeastern United States. They lack hind limbs and can grow up to three feet long.

name: Three-Toed Amphiuma
funFact: Three-Toed Amphiumas have vestigial legs that are so small they are almost impossible to see.
description: The Three-Toed Amphiuma is a fully aquatic salamander found in the southeastern United States. It has an eel-like body with three tiny, non-functional toes on each vestigial limb.

name: Waterdog
habitat: Clear streams and rivers with rocky bottoms
funFact: Waterdogs retain their external gills throughout their lives, a condition known as neoteny.
description: The Waterdog is a fully aquatic salamander found in eastern North America. Like the mudpuppy, it retains its external gills throughout life and is an important indicator of stream health.

name: Spring Salamander
funFact: Spring Salamanders are one of the few salamander species that can live their entire lives in water.
description: The Spring Salamander is a large, robust salamander found in cold mountain streams of eastern North America. They have a distinctive salmon or orange coloration with dark reticulations.

name: Cave Salamander
habitat: Caves, springs, and moist rocky areas
funFact: Cave Salamanders can climb vertical rock faces using their specialized toe pads.
description: The Cave Salamander is a brightly colored salamander with orange to red body and black spots. Found in caves and rocky areas of the eastern United States, they are excellent climbers.

name: Arboreal Salamander
funFact: Arboreal Salamanders can climb trees and have prehensile tails for gripping branches.
description: The Arboreal Salamander is a lungless salamander found in the coastal mountains of California. They are excellent climbers, spending much of their time in oak trees and rock crevices.

name: Ensatina
funFact: Ensatina salamanders form a ring species around California's Central Valley, with different subspecies at each end.
description: The Ensatina is a colorful salamander found along the Pacific coast of North America. They are famous in evolutionary biology as an example of a ring species, with different color morphs forming a circle around California's Central Valley.

name: Slender Salamander
funFact: Slender Salamanders can coil into a tight spiral to conserve moisture.
description: The Slender Salamander is a small, lungless salamander found in California. They have long, thin bodies and can coil into a spiral when disturbed or to prevent water loss.

name: Ringed Salamander
funFact: Ringed Salamanders migrate to breed during autumn rains, one of the few fall-breeding amphibians.
description: The Ringed Salamander is a large, dark salamander with yellow or white rings or spots. Found in the Ozark Plateau region of the United States, they are one of the few salamanders that breed in the fall.

name: Flatwoods Salamander
habitat: Longleaf pine flatwoods and seasonal ponds
funFact: Flatwoods Salamanders have a distinctive dark crossband pattern that helps them camouflage on the forest floor.
description: The Flatwoods Salamander is a small, threatened salamander found in the longleaf pine forests of the southeastern United States. They breed in temporary fishless ponds and are declining due to habitat loss.

name: Dusky Salamander
funFact: Dusky Salamanders can autotomize their tails when threatened, which continue to wiggle and distract predators.
description: The Dusky Salamander is a medium-sized lungless salamander found in eastern North America. They are variable in color and pattern and are often found near streams and springs.

name: Four-Toed Salamander
funFact: Four-Toed Salamanders have only four toes on their hind feet, unlike most salamanders which have five.
description: The Four-Toed Salamander is a small salamander found in bogs and wetlands of eastern North America. They are the only salamander in their range with four toes on their hind feet.

name: Gulf Coast Salamander
funFact: Gulf Coast Salamanders are one of the few salamander species that can tolerate slightly brackish water.
description: The Gulf Coast Salamander is a small salamander found in the coastal lowlands of the southeastern United States. They are often found in bottomland hardwood forests and can tolerate mildly saline conditions.

name: Tropical Caecilian
habitat: Tropical rainforest soils and leaf litter
funFact: Caecilians are often mistaken for snakes or worms, but they are actually limbless amphibians.
description: Tropical Caecilians are limbless, serpentine amphibians found in tropical regions of the world. They live underground or in leaf litter, feeding on small invertebrates, and are the least known order of amphibians.

name: Boulenger's Caecilian
funFact: Boulenger's Caecilians have minute vestigial eyes that can detect light but not form images.
description: Boulenger's Caecilian is one of the largest caecilian species, found in South America. These burrowing amphibians have ring-like grooves along their body and tiny, non-functional eyes buried beneath the skin.

name: Ringed Caecilian
habitat: Moist tropical soils and agricultural areas
funFact: Ringed Caecilians have a unique sensory organ called a tentacle that helps them detect prey underground.
description: The Ringed Caecilian is a limbless amphibian found in South America and the Caribbean. They have a distinctive ring-like pattern on their body and use a chemosensory tentacle to find prey in the soil.

name: Monarch Butterfly
habitat: Meadows, fields, and gardens across North America
funFact: Monarchs migrate up to 3,000 miles from Canada to Mexico each fall.
description: The monarch butterfly is one of the most recognizable butterflies in North America, known for its striking orange and black wing pattern. It is famous for its incredible long-distance migration across thousands of miles.

name: Luna Moth
habitat: Deciduous hardwood forests of North America
funFact: Luna moths do not have mouths and cannot eat as adults, living only on stored energy.
description: The luna moth is a large, pale green moth with long tail-like hindwings. It is nocturnal and attracted to light, and adults do not feed, dedicating their brief adult lives entirely to reproduction.

name: Atlas Moth
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests of Southeast Asia
funFact: The atlas moth is one of the largest insects in the world by wing area.
description: The atlas moth is the largest moth species, with a wingspan that can exceed 12 inches. Its wings have snake-head-shaped tips that deter predators, and like other giant moths, adults do not feed.

name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail
funFact: Female swallowtails can mimic the toxic pipevine swallowtail to avoid predators.
description: The eastern tiger swallowtail is a large, bright yellow butterfly with distinctive black tiger stripes. It is one of the most common and recognizable butterflies in eastern North America.

name: Hawk Moth
habitat: Gardens, woodlands, and tropical forests worldwide
funFact: Hawk moths are among the fastest flying insects, capable of hovering like hummingbirds.
description: Hawk moths, also known as sphinx moths, are powerful fliers with streamlined bodies. Many species have extremely long proboscises for feeding on deep-throated flowers while hovering.

name: Painted Lady Butterfly
habitat: Meadows, gardens, and open fields worldwide
funFact: Painted ladies migrate across the Sahara Desert and the Mediterranean Sea.
description: The painted lady is one of the most widespread butterflies on Earth, found on every continent except Antarctica. It is a strong migrant and a common visitor to gardens.

name: Blue Morpho Butterfly
habitat: Tropical rainforests of Central and South America
funFact: The morpho's blue color is not pigment but structural coloration from microscopic scales.
description: The blue morpho is a brilliantly iridescent blue butterfly found in tropical rainforests. Its metallic blue wings are visible from great distances and are produced by light diffraction rather than pigment.

name: Glasswing Butterfly
funFact: The glasswing butterfly has nearly transparent wings due to nanopillar structures.
description: The glasswing butterfly has remarkably transparent wings with only a thin dark border. The transparency is caused by tiny nanopillar structures on the wings that prevent light reflection.

name: Cecropia Moth
habitat: Deciduous forests of eastern North America
funFact: The cecropia moth is the largest native moth in North America.
description: The cecropia moth is North America's largest moth with wingspans reaching 7 inches. It has striking red, orange, and white markings and, like other giant moths, adults do not feed.

name: Io Moth
habitat: Deciduous forests and shrublands of eastern North America
funFact: Each wing of the io moth has a large, striking eyespot that deters predators.
description: The io moth is a beautiful silk moth with large eyespots on each wing. Males are yellow while females are reddish-brown, and both sexes flash their eyespots when threatened.

name: Polyphemus Moth
habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests of North America
funFact: The polyphemus moth is named after the one-eyed Greek giant Polyphemus.
description: The polyphemus moth is a large, tan-colored silk moth with distinctive eyespots on its hindwings. It is named after the Cyclops of Greek mythology due to the large eyespots.

name: Viceroy Butterfly
funFact: Viceroys mimic the toxic monarch butterfly for protection from predators.
description: The viceroy butterfly closely resembles the monarch and was long thought to be a mimic. It is now known to be somewhat distasteful to predators, making it a Müllerian mimic.

name: Red Admiral Butterfly
funFact: Red admirals are territorial and will chase other butterflies from their favorite basking spots.
description: The red admiral is a striking black butterfly with bold red-orange bands and white spots. It is a strong flier found worldwide and often visits rotting fruit and tree sap.

name: Great Spangled Fritillary
funFact: Fritillary caterpillars feed exclusively on violets, which is how the group got its name.
description: The great spangled fritillary is a large, orange butterfly with distinctive silver-spotted underwings. Its larvae feed on various violet species while adults nectar on milkweed and coneflowers.

name: Clouded Yellow
habitat: Meadows, pastures, and farmland across Europe and Asia
funFact: Clouded yellows are strong migrants that can travel hundreds of miles.
description: The clouded yellow is a bright golden butterfly common across Europe and parts of Asia. It is a strong migratory species that sometimes appears in large numbers in areas outside its normal range.

name: Comma Butterfly
funFact: The comma butterfly is named for the small white comma-shaped mark on its underwings.
description: The comma butterfly has uniquely ragged wing edges that help camouflage it as a dead leaf. It has a distinctive white comma-shaped mark on its dark brown underwings.

name: Mourning Cloak Butterfly
funFact: The mourning cloak is one of the longest-lived butterflies and overwinters as an adult.
description: The mourning cloak is one of the longest-lived butterflies, surviving up to 11 months. It overwinters as an adult and is often the first butterfly seen in spring, with dark wings bordered in yellow.

name: Zebra Longwing Butterfly
funFact: Zebra longwings are the state butterfly of Florida and can live on pollen alone.
description: The zebra longwing is a distinctive butterfly with black wings marked by pale yellow stripes. It is unique among butterflies in that adults can digest pollen, extending their lifespan significantly.
region: Southern United States, Central America, and South America

name: Snowflake Butterfly
habitat: Tropical forests of Central and South America
funFact: The snowflake butterfly has mostly white wings with delicate black tips.
description: The snowflake butterfly is a delicate white butterfly found in tropical forests. Its mostly white wings with small dark tips give it a graceful appearance as it glides through forest understory.

name: Resurrection Butterfly
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests of East Asia
funFact: The resurrection butterfly is considered a symbol of rebirth in Japanese culture.
description: The resurrection butterfly, known as Kuroneko Yamane in Japan, is a medium-sized butterfly with distinctive markings. It has deep cultural significance in Japan as a symbol of love and resurrection.

name: Small White Butterfly
habitat: Gardens, farmlands, and disturbed areas worldwide
funFact: The small white is one of the most common butterflies in the world and a notorious garden pest.
description: The small white butterfly is a widespread species often found in gardens and agricultural areas. Its caterpillars are major pests of cabbage and other brassica crops.

name: Atlas Beetle
funFact: Atlas beetles can carry objects 850 times their own body weight.
description: The atlas beetle is a large rhinoceros beetle native to Southeast Asian rainforests. Males have three prominent horns used in combat for mates, and they are among the strongest insects relative to size.

name: Goliath Beetle
habitat: Tropical rainforests and savannas of Africa
funFact: Goliath beetles are among the heaviest insects in the world.
description: The goliath beetle is one of the largest and heaviest insects on Earth, found in African tropical forests. They feed on fruit and tree sap, and their larvae are among the heaviest grubs known.

name: Western Hercules Beetle
funFact: Rhinoceros beetles can lift objects 850 times their own body weight.
description: The western hercules beetle is a large rhinoceros beetle found in the hardwood forests of North America. Males have a distinctive horn used for wrestling other males during mating season.

name: Stag Beetle
funFact: Male stag beetles use their enormous mandibles to wrestle rivals for mates.
description: Stag beetles are named for the large, antler-like mandibles of the males. They spend most of their lives as larvae feeding on decaying wood underground before emerging as impressive adults.

name: Common Eastern Firefly
funFact: Firefly larvae glow too, and some produce light to deter predators.
description: Fireflies are beetles famous for their bioluminescent abdomens used to attract mates. Both adults and larvae produce light through a chemical reaction involving luciferin and luciferase.

name: Scarab Dung Beetle
funFact: Dung beetles navigate using the Milky Way, the first insects found to use stars.
description: Dung beetles roll animal droppings into balls for food or breeding. They are essential decomposers that help recycle nutrients back into the soil and reduce parasite populations in pastures.

name: Seven-Spotted Ladybug
funFact: A single ladybug can eat up to 5,000 aphids in its lifetime.
description: Ladybugs are small, round beetles valued by gardeners for their appetite for aphids and other plant pests. Their bright red coloration with black spots warns predators of their bitter taste.

name: Six-Spotted Tiger Beetle
habitat: Sandy paths, mudflats, and forest edges
funFact: Tiger beetles run so fast they go temporarily blind because their eyes cannot process images quickly enough.
description: Tiger beetles are fast-running predatory beetles with large eyes and powerful jaws. They are voracious hunters of smaller insects and are often found on open, sunlit ground.

name: Asian Longhorned Beetle
funFact: The Asian longhorned beetle can kill healthy hardwood trees by tunneling through their bark.
description: The Asian longhorned beetle is an invasive species that attacks a wide variety of hardwood trees. It has distinctive black and white markings and very long antennae that exceed its body length.
region: East Asia (invasive in North America and Europe)

name: Click Beetle
funFact: Click beetles can launch themselves into the air with a clicking mechanism without using their legs.
description: Click beetles have a unique clicking mechanism on their thorax that allows them to snap and launch into the air when overturned. Their larvae, called wireworms, are important soil dwellers.

name: Bombardier Beetle
funFact: Bombardier beetles spray a boiling chemical spray at 212 degrees Fahrenheit from their abdomen.
description: The bombardier beetle defends itself by ejecting a hot, noxious chemical spray from its abdomen with an audible pop. The spray reaches temperatures near boiling and repels predators effectively.

name: June Bug
funFact: June bugs are clumsy fliers and often bounce off windows and walls.
description: June bugs are chunky, brown beetles that emerge in late spring. They are attracted to lights at night and their larvae, known as white grubs, feed on grass roots and can damage lawns.

name: Whirligig Beetle
funFact: Whirligig beetles have four eyes: two for seeing above water and two for seeing below.
description: Whirligig beetles are aquatic beetles that spin rapidly on the surface of calm water. They have split eyes adapted for both aerial and aquatic vision and are social insects that form groups.

name: Predaceous Diving Beetle
funFact: Diving beetles carry an air bubble under their wing covers to breathe underwater.
description: Predaceous diving beetles are streamlined aquatic predators that hunt tadpoles, small fish, and other insects underwater. They trap air beneath their elytra for extended submerged hunting.

name: Oil Beetle
funFact: Oil beetles secrete oily droplets from their joints that repel predators and can blister human skin.
description: Oil beetles are flightless blister beetles that produce cantharidin, a toxic oily substance, from their joints. Their larvae parasitize solitary bees and develop inside their nests.

name: Bess Beetle
habitat: Decaying logs and stumps in forests
funFact: Bess beetles communicate by rubbing their abdomen to make squeaking sounds.
description: Bess beetles are large, shiny black beetles that live in decaying wood. They exhibit parental care, with adults feeding and caring for their larvae, which is unusual for beetles.

name: Mountain Pine Beetle
funFact: Mountain pine beetle outbreaks can kill millions of acres of forest in a single year.
description: Mountain pine beetles are tiny bark beetles that bore into pine trees and introduce blue-stain fungi. Massive outbreaks have devastated millions of acres of forest in western North America.

name: Sacred Scarab Beetle
habitat: Grasslands and pastures of Africa and Mediterranean
funFact: Ancient Egyptians revered the scarab as a symbol of the sun god Khepri.
description: The sacred scarab beetle rolls dung into balls and was revered in ancient Egyptian culture as a symbol of rebirth and the sun's daily journey across the sky.

name: American Carrion Beetle
habitat: Forests and areas with decaying matter
funFact: Carrion beetles can locate a dead animal from over a mile away using chemical sensors.
description: The American carrion beetle is a large, flat beetle that feeds on dead animals and snails. It plays an important ecological role in recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

name: Patrol Bess Beetle
funFact: Patrol bess beetles produce sounds by rubbing ridges on their abdomen when disturbed.
description: The patrol bess beetle is a large, glossy black beetle found in tropical rainforests. Like other passalid beetles, both parents work together to feed and care for their larvae.

name: Eyed Click Beetle
funFact: The eyed click beetle has two large eyespots on its thorax that startle predators.
description: The eyed click beetle is a large click beetle with distinctive eyespots on its pronotum. When threatened, it clicks and flips into the air to right itself or escape danger.

name: Rose Chafer
funFact: Rose chafers can fly with their elytra closed, using only their hind wings.
description: The rose chafer is a metallic green beetle that feeds on flowers, especially roses and fruit blossoms. Despite being considered a pest, its larvae help decompose organic matter in soil.

name: Japanese Beetle
funFact: Japanese beetles release aggregation pheromones that attract more beetles to feed.
description: The Japanese beetle is a highly invasive pest that skeletonizes leaves and damages turf with its white grub larvae. It is native to Japan and has become a devastating pest in North America.
region: East Asia (invasive in North America and Europe)

name: Colorado Potato Beetle
habitat: Potato fields and solanaceous crop areas
funFact: The Colorado potato beetle is one of the most insecticide-resistant pests in the world.
description: The Colorado potato beetle is a major agricultural pest that feeds on potatoes, tomatoes, and eggplants. It has developed resistance to over 50 different insecticides.

name: Scarlet Lily Beetle
funFact: Lily beetles are bright red, making them easy to spot on green leaves.
description: The scarlet lily beetle is a bright red pest of lily plants. Both adults and larvae feed on leaves, stems, and flowers, and the larvae cover themselves in their own excrement for protection.

name: Elm Leaf Beetle
habitat: Near elm trees in urban and suburban areas
funFact: Elm leaf beetles can enter homes through small cracks and hibernate indoors during winter.
description: The elm leaf beetle skeletonizes elm tree leaves and is a significant urban pest. Adults often overwinter inside buildings, emerging in spring to feed on newly emerged elm leaves.

name: Red Imported Fire Ant
funFact: Fire ant colonies can form living rafts that float on water for weeks during floods.
description: Red imported fire ants are invasive ants native to South America that deliver painful stings causing burning welts. They build large mound nests and can survive flooding by forming floating colonies.

name: Leafcutter Ant
habitat: Tropical forests of Central and South America
funFact: Leafcutter ants are the largest consumers of vegetation in the Neotropics.
description: Leafcutter ants cut and carry pieces of leaves back to their nests to feed a special fungus that they cultivate. They are sophisticated farmers with complex division of labor among castes.

name: Bullet Ant
habitat: Lowland rainforests of Central and South America
funFact: The bullet ant's sting is rated as the most painful insect sting in the world.
description: The bullet ant gets its name from the intense pain of its sting, which has been compared to being shot. Indigenous tribes use bullet ant stings in coming-of-age rituals.

name: Army Ant
habitat: Tropical forests of Africa and the Americas
funFact: Army ant colonies of millions move in massive raiding columns that devour everything in their path.
description: Army ants are nomadic predators that form massive raiding swarms. They do not build permanent nests but instead form living bivouacs made of their own bodies while the colony rests.

name: Trap-Jaw Ant
habitat: Tropical forests of Southeast Asia and the Americas
funFact: Trap-jaw ants can snap their mandibles at speeds exceeding 140 mph.
description: Trap-jaw ants have spring-loaded mandibles that snap shut at incredible speeds to capture prey and can also use the force to launch themselves into the air to escape predators.

name: Weaver Ant
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests of Asia and Australia
funFact: Weaver ants use their own larvae as living glue guns to stitch leaves together.
description: Weaver ants build elaborate nests by weaving living leaves together using silk produced by their larvae. They are aggressive defenders of their territory and tend honeydew-producing insects.

name: Western Honeybee
habitat: Meadows, gardens, and agricultural areas worldwide
funFact: A single honeybee colony can visit over 225,000 flowers to produce one pound of honey.
description: The western honeybee is the world's most important pollinator of agricultural crops. They live in highly organized colonies with complex social structures and produce honey and beeswax.

name: Common Bumblebee
funFact: Bumblebees can fly in colder temperatures than most bees due to their ability to thermoregulate.
description: Bumblebees are robust, fuzzy bees important for pollinating wildflowers and crops. They are capable of buzz pollination, vibrating their flight muscles to release pollen from flowers.

name: Eastern Carpenter Bee
habitat: Forests, gardens, and near wooden structures
funFact: Carpenter bees drill perfectly round holes in wood to create nesting galleries.
description: Carpenter bees are large, solitary bees that bore into untreated wood to create nesting tunnels. Despite their intimidating size, they are gentle and rarely sting, preferring to hover near structures.

name: European Paper Wasp
funFact: Paper wasps build their nests from chewed wood fibers mixed with saliva.
description: Paper wasps are slender wasps with long legs that build open-comb umbrella-shaped nests from wood pulp. They are beneficial predators of caterpillars but will sting if their nest is threatened.

name: Common Yellow Jacket
funFact: Yellow jacket colonies can grow to contain 4,000 or more workers by late summer.
description: Yellow jackets are aggressive wasps known for their bright yellow and black markings. They build enclosed paper nests and are notorious for scavenging at picnics and outdoor events.

name: Bald-Faced Hornet
habitat: Forests and suburban areas of eastern North America
funFact: Bald-faced hornets can spray venom from their stingers up to several feet.
description: Despite its name, the bald-faced hornet is actually a yellowjacket, not a true hornet. It builds large, enclosed paper nests high in trees and is known for its aggressive defense of its colony.

name: European Hornet
funFact: European hornets are attracted to light and will often fly into homes at night.
description: The European hornet is the largest social wasp in Europe and an invasive species in North America. Queens can reach 1.4 inches in length, and colonies can contain up to 1,000 workers.

name: Tarantula Hawk Wasp
habitat: Deserts and scrublands of the Americas
funFact: The tarantula hawk has one of the most painful insect stings in the world.
description: The tarantula hawk is a large, metallic blue-black wasp that hunts tarantulas to serve as live food for its larvae. Its sting is excruciatingly painful but rarely dangerous to humans.

name: Cuckoo Wasp
habitat: Sandy areas and near host bee nests
funFact: Cuckoo wasps can curl into a ball when threatened, using their armored exoskeleton for protection.
description: Cuckoo wasps are brilliant metallic blue or green parasitoids that lay their eggs in the nests of other bees and wasps. Their larvae consume the host's eggs or larvae and stored food.

name: Giant Ichneumon Wasp
habitat: Forests with dead or dying trees
funFact: The giant ichneumon's ovipositor can be longer than its body and drills through wood to reach beetle larvae.
description: Giant ichneumon wasps are parasitoids that use their extremely long ovipositors to drill into wood and lay eggs inside wood-boring beetle larvae. Despite their fearsome appearance, they cannot sting humans.

name: Asian Giant Hornet
habitat: Forests and mountains of East Asia
funFact: The Asian giant hornet can decapitate an entire honeybee colony in hours.
description: The Asian giant hornet, nicknamed the murder hornet, is the world's largest hornet. Its powerful sting delivers potent venom and it is a devastating predator of honeybee colonies.

name: Sweat Bee
funFact: Some sweat bees have metallic green or blue bodies that shimmer in the sunlight.
description: Sweat bees are small, often metallic-colored bees attracted to human perspiration for its salt content. They are important pollinators and nest in the ground or in hollow stems.

name: Blue Orchard Mason Bee
funFact: Mason bees are 100 times more efficient at pollinating than honeybees.
description: The blue orchard mason bee is a solitary bee that nests in hollow tubes and crevices. It is a far more efficient pollinator than honeybees, visiting far more flowers per hour.

name: Tawny Mining Bee
funFact: Mining bees create small volcano-shaped mounds of soil at their nest entrances.
description: Mining bees are solitary ground-nesting bees that excavate tunnels in soil. They emerge in spring and are important early-season pollinators of fruit trees and wildflowers.

name: Golden Digger Wasp
funFact: Golden digger wasps paralyze grasshoppers and crickets to feed their larvae alive.
description: The golden digger wasp is a large, metallic golden wasp that hunts grasshoppers and crickets. It buries paralyzed prey in underground nests for its developing larvae.

name: Mud Dauber Wasp
funFact: Mud daubers stock their nests with paralyzed spiders for their developing larvae.
description: Mud dauber wasps are solitary wasps that construct tubular mud nests on sheltered surfaces. They hunt and paralyze spiders to stock each cell for their developing young.

name: Horned Mason Bee
habitat: Woodlands and gardens with hollow stems
funFact: Male horned mason bees have small horns on their faces used in mating displays.
description: The horned mason bee is a solitary bee that nests in hollow stems and bee hotels. Males have distinctive facial horns and both sexes are important early-season pollinators.

name: Wool Carder Bee
funFact: Wool carder bees scrape plant hairs to line their nests, hence their name.
description: Wool carder bees are solitary bees that collect plant hairs to line their nest cells. Males aggressively defend patches of fuzzy plants where females forage for nesting material.

name: Cicada Killer Wasp
habitat: Sandy soils and sunny areas near trees
funFact: The cicada killer is the largest wasp in North America and can be over 2 inches long.
description: The cicada killer is a massive solitary wasp that hunts cicadas to provision its underground nest. Despite its intimidating size, it rarely stings humans unless provoked.

name: Red Velvet Ant
funFact: The velvet ant is actually a wingless wasp with one of the most painful stings in the insect world.
description: The red velvet ant is a wingless female wasp with a dense covering of bright red hairs. Despite its ant-like appearance, it is a parasitoid wasp whose sting is extremely painful.

name: Cuckoo Bumblebee
funFact: Cuckoo bumblebees infiltrate other bumblebee nests and lay their eggs for the host to raise.
description: Cuckoo bumblebees are social parasites that take over the nests of other bumblebee species. The female cuckoo bumblebee displaces the host queen and lays her own eggs for the workers to tend.

name: Asian Tiger Mosquito
habitat: Urban and suburban areas, standing water
funFact: Only female mosquitoes bite, needing blood protein to produce eggs.
description: The Asian tiger mosquito is an invasive species that can transmit dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses. It is identified by its distinctive black and white striped body and legs.

name: Common House Fly
habitat: Near human habitation and livestock worldwide
funFact: House flies taste with their feet and can detect food from miles away.
description: The common house fly is one of the most widespread insects, closely associated with humans. It has sponging mouthparts for liquid feeding and can transmit numerous diseases.

name: Common Fruit Fly
habitat: Near rotting fruit and fermented foods
funFact: Fruit flies are one of the most important model organisms in genetics research.
description: The common fruit fly is tiny but remarkably important in scientific research. They reproduce rapidly and share many genes with humans, making them invaluable for studying genetics and disease.

name: Crane Fly
funFact: Crane flies are often mistakenly called giant mosquitoes but do not bite or suck blood.
description: Crane flies are delicate, long-legged insects that resemble oversized mosquitoes. Adults are harmless and many do not feed at all, while their larvae, known as leatherjackets, live in soil.

name: Horse Fly
habitat: Near water, marshes, and livestock areas
funFact: Horse flies are among the fastest flying insects, reaching speeds up to 90 mph.
description: Horse flies are large, powerful fliers with razor-sharp mouthparts that slash skin to feed on blood. Only females bite, and their painful bites can transmit diseases to livestock and humans.

name: Human Bot Fly
funFact: Bot fly larvae develop under human skin, creating painful boils called myiasis.
description: The human bot fly is a parasitic insect whose larvae develop beneath the skin of mammals, including humans. Adults do not bite; instead, they hijack mosquitoes to deliver their eggs to hosts.

name: Common Hover Fly
funFact: Hover flies mimic bees and wasps for protection but are completely harmless.
description: Hover flies are beneficial pollinators that mimic the appearance of stinging insects for protection. Their larvae are important predators of aphids, making them valuable in pest control.

name: Black Fly
funFact: Black fly swarms can be so dense that they suffocate livestock by blocking their airways.
description: Black flies are tiny but relentless biting insects that breed in flowing water. In some regions they transmit river blindness and are considered one of the most important disease vectors.

name: Common Green Darner
funFact: Dragonflies can fly in all six directions and hover like a helicopter.
description: Dragonflies are ancient aerial predators with enormous compound eyes and two pairs of independently controlled wings. They are among the most efficient hunters in the insect world.

name: Blue-Tailed Damselfly
funFact: Damselflies fold their wings along their bodies when at rest, unlike dragonflies.
description: Damselflies are slender, delicate relatives of dragonflies that hold their wings together above their body when resting. They are important aquatic ecosystem indicators and voracious mosquito predators.

name: Blue Dasher Dragonfly
funFact: Blue dashers can fly backwards and hover in place like a helicopter.
description: The blue dasher is a small, common dragonfly with a blue-green body and distinctive wing pattern. It is an agile aerial predator that catches mosquitoes and other small insects on the wing.

name: Emperor Dragonfly
funFact: Emperor dragonflies can eat their own body weight in insects every day.
